result.title: Backbone-Specific LoRA Geometry: Orthogonality, Superposition, and Provenance
result.summary: Sharing one low-rank adaptation (LoRA) update across pretrained models simplifies deployment. Composition methods typically combine updates from a common backbone, while cross-model transfer transforms updates for a target backbone. The conditions for sharing updates across backbones while preserving accuracy and distinguishing individual contributions remain unclear. Our idea is to use backbone-specific update directions as signatures of their training backbones. We derive a cross-backbone correlation bound from attention symmetries and equivariant LoRA learning under independent, uniform pretrained feature orientations. A local gradient-flow model explains positive mean correlation between independent runs on the same backbone and task. These patterns motivate cosine-based backbone identification and inner-product tests for registered-adapter reuse without coordinate alignment. Experiments on CLIP backbones show that shared sums achieve nearly the same mean accuracy as separate adapters. Cosine scores reliably identify source backbones across the evaluated tasks. Registered adapters remain detectable in sums of adapters from different backbones.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究跨 CLIP backbone 共享 LoRA 更新的条件，论证不同 backbone 的更新方向可作为「来源签名」，并提出基于余弦相似度的 backbone 识别与内积检验，用于免坐标对齐地复用和追溯 adapter。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于低秩更新的正交性、叠加与来源可辨识性的分析，可能为核查 latent 状态叠加、多源贡献归属及无需对齐的相似度比较提供几何视角，但对象是参数空间而非推理状态，迁移需较多核查。
